Official structure

ESOL Reading Entry 2: qualification overview

Understand the Award, its single mandatory unit, assessment method and progression routes before you practise.

Assessment

How the four-task reading assessment works

Use the current sample assessor guidance to plan one hour without inventing a fixed question count.

Reading skill

Recognise a text's purpose and layout

Decide whether a text informs, instructs, warns, invites or asks before you search for detail.

Everyday texts

Read signs and notices accurately

Turn short public messages into the correct action by combining wording, symbols and context.

Practical reading

Navigate forms, lists and alphabetical order

Locate the right field, row or name without confusing labels with the information entered beside them.

Practical reading

Follow instructions and put steps in order

Use sequence markers, pronouns and cause-and-effect language to rebuild the correct process.

Everyday texts

Read messages, emails and short letters

Identify sender, recipient, reason, time and requested response in everyday communication.

Vocabulary

Work out vocabulary from context

Use nearby definitions, examples, contrasts and word families before reaching for a dictionary.

Reading skill

Separate the main idea from supporting detail

Summarise what a short text is mainly about, then locate the exact evidence for detailed questions.

Reading skill

Make a simple inference without guessing

Combine two clear clues to reach a practical conclusion that the text supports.

Assessment strategy

Use the permitted dictionary and your hour well

Apply the sample guidance on dictionary use, task order and 15-minute guide times.

Study plan

A six-week ESOL Reading Entry 2 plan

Move from everyday text recognition to full four-task practice with focused error review.
